collections.title: The Thanksgiving Table Edit
collections.headline: Cream and amber, layered so the food is the only color on the table
collections.intro: Thanksgiving at its most classic is a table that gets out of the way: cream stoneware, a linen runner down the length of the table, ivory napkins, amber glass catching the candlelight. Nothing here competes with the bird, which is why the same plates will look right at Easter and on an ordinary Tuesday in March. It is built in the order a table is actually set, plates first, then linen, then light.
collections.art_note: A long dining table shot from a high three quarter angle in late afternoon window light: a light natural linen runner running the full length and pooling at the near end, cream stoneware dinner plates set on round water hyacinth chargers, ivory cotton napkins folded loose beside each plate with one Spode Woodland turkey plate tucked under a cream plate as the single patterned note, amber pressed glass goblets and amber hobnail tumblers catching the light, a white ceramic serving bowl of mashed potatoes and a wide shallow bowl of stuffing at the center, three gold taper holders at three heights with ivory beeswax tapers lit, a loose bundle of faux eucalyptus laid along the runner and two potted eucalyptus in cream pots at the far end. Cream, ivory, natural flax, amber and one warm honey flame, soft directional daylight with long shadows across the wood, no people, no text

collections.title: The Moody Thanksgiving Edit
collections.headline: Black matte, wine and brass, with the candles doing the lighting
collections.intro: A moody table starts with black: matte stoneware plates, a dark brown linen runner, burgundy cotton napkins and smoke gray glass, then brass candle holders short enough that the flames sit below the conversation. There is almost no color anywhere except the wine and one low arrangement of burgundy peonies, and that restraint is what makes the room read as deliberate. This is the set for the year you host after dark, when the table has to hold its own against the candles.
collections.art_note: A Thanksgiving table shot at a low three quarter angle in a dark room, lit by candles only: black matte stoneware dinner plates and coupe settings, a dark brown linen runner running the full length with a shorter wine hemstitch runner laid over it, burgundy cotton napkins beside each plate, smoke gray ribbed goblets and stemless glasses with a copper band, three short antique brass candlesticks holding lit burgundy beeswax tapers, a reversible acacia board with bread at the center and a glass carafe beside it, four burgundy peony stems kept low in a footed bowl. Black, burgundy, dark brown and antique brass, deep shadow with warm flame cores and one copper highlight, no people, no text

collections.title: The Thanksgiving Hosting Edit
collections.headline: The table is set before the first guest knocks
collections.intro: Thanksgiving is won in the hour before anyone sits down: the platter that fits the bird, the board that keeps people out of the kitchen, the candles that make a buffet look deliberate. Nothing here is themed, which is why it all still works on a Tuesday.
collections.art_note: A hosted Thanksgiving table at warm golden hour, camera slightly above and to the side, looking along a cream linen cloth: an acacia charcuterie board with aged cheese, dark grapes and rosemary, a hand woven rattan bread basket lined with linen, a large oval cream platter with two plain side plates, a cream and deep green glazed ceramic pumpkin dish, three lit ivory tapers in dark wood candlesticks, two amber glass votives, a hurricane glass holder, a pale green pressed glass tumbler, folded cream napkins in carved acacia rings, antique brass flatware. Cream, amber, acacia, sage and terracotta in raking afternoon light, no people, no text.

collections.title: The Thanksgiving Welcome Edit
collections.headline: What the porch says before the door opens
collections.intro: This is everything a guest meets before they are inside: a wreath on the door, a plaid mat that can take wet boots, a pair of urns either side of the step, baskets for whatever lands by the entrance and dried stems to carry the season a little further. It is twelve pieces, not a whole house, and it is meant to be finished in an afternoon. Set it once and it holds from the first cold week through the last of the leaves.
collections.art_note: A front porch shot straight on from the path, camera at chest height: a magnolia leaf and pine wreath hung on a dark painted door with a smaller eucalyptus wreath on the porch wall beside it, a black and white buffalo plaid mat on the step below, two black fluted urn planters flanking the door with rust mums in them, a tall water hyacinth basket of folded throws beside the nearer urn, a stone urn on the step holding a hand tied dried bouquet, two woven cattail pumpkins at the base of the planters and a bundle of dried pampas in a floor vase at the edge of the frame. Warm beige, black, natural green and rust, low late afternoon sun raking across the porch boards, no people, no text
